products.title: Aurora Smart 78 — RGB App-Controlled LED
products.body_html:
A 34W RGB LED bar for planted freshwater tanks, set from your phone. 4200 lumens at CRI 90Ra across a 78 cm span, with two bracket heights in the box covering tanks from 70 cm to 95 cm long.

  • Full colour, set from your phone. RGB mixing across the spectrum, adjusted in an app rather than by cycling a button on the cord.
  • Colour you can judge plants by. CRI 90Ra means greens read as greens. Cheap aquarium LEDs sit in the 70s and make a planted tank look flat.
  • 4200 lumens over 78 cm — the second-brightest in the series. Output for every length is in the gallery.
  • Two bracket heights included. Short legs for tanks 70–80 cm, tall legs for 80–95 cm.
  • Aluminium body, IP44 splash rated. Built for the splashes and condensation of an open-top tank, not for submersion.

faqs.q: What size tank does this suit?
faqs.a: The bar is 78 cm long. With the low bracket it suits tanks 70–80 cm long, and with the high bracket 80–95 cm. Both brackets are in the box. On a 95 cm tank the ends of the scape will be noticeably dimmer.

faqs.q: Is 4200 lumens enough for carpeting plants?
faqs.a: For most carpets at this span, yes. We do not publish a PAR figure because the manufacturer does not measure one, and we will not estimate it. If you are growing something genuinely demanding, ask us first.

faqs.q: How is the colour controlled?
faqs.a: Through a phone app over the light's own wireless link. Set the RGB mix once and the fixture keeps it.

faqs.q: Can it get wet?
faqs.a: It is IP44, which covers splashing and condensation on an open-top tank. It is not submersible. An earlier version of this listing claimed IP68 — that was wrong and we have corrected it.

faqs.q: Does it do a sunrise and sunset ramp?
faqs.a: The manufacturer documents no scheduled ramp for this model, so we do not claim one. What is confirmed is app-based colour and brightness control.

products.title: Aurora 48 Planted Tank LED Bar
products.body_html:
A 20W full-spectrum LED bar for planted freshwater tanks between 48 and 58 cm wide (19–23 in). Forty LEDs — thirty daylight white and ten actinic blue — on a retractable bracket, running 90–260V so the same unit works on Australian and US mains.

  • It fits the tank you already own. The bracket slides 10 cm, so one bar covers 48–58 cm of rim. Measure the outside width of the rim, not the water line, and check it against the range before ordering.
  • One unit, either country. 90–260V universal input. No transformer and no voltage-specific variant to get wrong — only the plug head differs.
  • Three modes on an inline switch. All-white for viewing and plant growth, blue-and-white together, or blue alone for a night tank.
  • A timer that repeats. Set the on/off time once and it repeats daily, so light stays consistent while you are away — the main defence against algae from an erratic photoperiod.
  • Slim enough to disappear. A low-profile bar that sits above the rim rather than dominating the tank, in white with translucent blue end caps.

Choosing between lengths. The series runs 18 cm to 58 cm and scales 8W to 24W. Pick by rim width rather than tank volume — a 48 cm bar on a 60 cm tank leaves the ends of the scape visibly dim.

faqs.q: Will this fit my tank?
faqs.a: It fits rims from 48 cm to 61 cm (19–24 in). The bar itself is 48 cm and the bracket adds up to 13 cm of travel. Measure the outside width of the rim, not the water line. If your tank is wider than 61 cm, choose the 58 cm model instead.

faqs.q: Will it work on Australian power?
faqs.a: Electrically yes — the driver accepts 90–260 V, so 240 V Australian mains is well within range. Check the plug type on your selected option before ordering; contact us if you need a specific plug and we will confirm what we can supply.

faqs.q: Is it bright enough to grow carpeting plants?
faqs.a: We do not publish a PAR figure for this light because the manufacturer does not provide one, and we will not invent one. What we can state is 20 W across 40 LEDs on a 48 cm bar. If you are growing demanding carpet species, treat this as a low-to-medium light and ask us before ordering.

faqs.q: Does it do a sunrise and sunset fade?
faqs.a: No. It has a repeating on/off timer and three switchable modes, not a gradual ramp. If you specifically want dawn-to-dusk fading, this is not the right fixture.

faqs.q: Can I leave the blue light on overnight?
faqs.a: Yes, the blue-only mode is intended for that. Bear in mind that continuous light of any colour contributes to algae, so most keepers run blue for a few evening hours rather than all night.

faqs.q: What is in the box?
faqs.a: The light bar with both brackets fitted, and the inline switch and power lead attached. No timer plug or wall adapter is included.

products.title: Light Timer Socket
products.body_html:
A plug-in mains timer for aquarium lights. One outlet, mechanical dial, rated to 2500 W at 250 V. Set the on and off times once and it repeats every day.

  • A consistent photoperiod is the cheapest algae control there is. Lights that go on and off at whatever hour you remember are one of the most common causes of an algae bloom in a new tank.
  • One outlet, one circuit. Plug the light in, set the dial, leave it.
  • Mechanical dial. No app, no menu, nothing to reconfigure after a power cut — but also no dimming and no sunrise ramp. See below.

faqs.q: Does this do a sunrise and sunset fade?
faqs.a: No. This listing previously claimed four channels and a 1–60 minute sunrise ramp. That was wrong. What our supplier ships is a single-outlet mechanical timer that switches a light fully on and fully off. We have corrected the listing and dropped the price accordingly.

faqs.q: Will it hold its settings in a power cut?
faqs.a: A mechanical dial keeps its programme, but the clock loses time while the power is out and will need resetting. We make no battery-backup claim because the manufacturer makes none.

products.title: DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless
products.body_html:
A refill-free CO2 kit for planted tanks. Citric acid and bicarbonate react inside a 2 L stainless bottle to produce CO2 — no gas cylinder, no trips to a refill shop.

  • No cylinder to refill. You top it up with two cheap dry chemicals instead of hauling a bottle to a gas supplier. That is the whole point of this design.
  • Constant-pressure valve body tested above 50 kg/cm² with a 3 kg regulated output and an automatic release above 30 kg.
  • Kit includes the 2 L stainless bottle, pressure gauge and valve, diffuser, 2 m of CO2 tubing, four suction cups, a 300 ml measuring cup, a funnel and two sets of reagent.

What this is not: a pressurised cylinder system. It is a chemical generator. Output tapers as the reaction exhausts and needs recharging every few weeks depending on your bubble rate. If you want set-and-forget pressurised CO2, buy a regulator and a refillable cylinder instead — this is the cheaper, more hands-on route.

images.alt: DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless

image.alt: DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless

faqs.q: Is this a pressurised CO2 system?
faqs.a: No, and this is the most important thing to understand before buying. It is a chemical generator: citric acid and bicarbonate react to make CO2. There is no cylinder to refill at a gas supplier, but output falls as the reaction exhausts and you recharge it every few weeks. This listing previously described it as a complete CO2 system at $129, which oversold it. We have corrected the description and the price.

faqs.q: How often does it need recharging?
faqs.a: Depends entirely on bubble rate and tank size — commonly two to four weeks on a small tank at a modest rate. The kit ships with two sets of reagent to start.

products.title: Aqua Soil — Planted Substrate, 9 L
products.body_html:
A baked aquasoil for planted tanks, sold by volume in a 9 L bag. Holds nutrients for root feeders and buffers water on the soft, acidic side that most aquarium plants prefer.

  • 9 L covers roughly a 60 cm tank at a usable planting depth of 5–6 cm, deeper at the back if you are terracing.
  • Feeds through the roots. Heavy root feeders — swords, crypts, most stems — do noticeably better in soil than in inert gravel.
  • Ships in the manufacturer's packaging. This is a third-party soil we resell rather than our own blend, and we are not going to pretend otherwise.

A note on weight: an earlier version of this listing said 20 lb. It is sold by volume, and 9 L of aquasoil weighs roughly 6 kg, not 9 kg.

faqs.q: How much do I need?
faqs.a: About 9 L for a 60 cm tank at 5–6 cm depth. Deeper if you are terracing toward the back.

faqs.q: Does it lower pH?
faqs.a: Aquasoils of this type generally buffer downward, but the manufacturer publishes no figure and we are not going to invent one. If you keep species with a narrow pH requirement, test as the tank settles.

products.title: Seiryu Stone — 5 kg Hardscape Pack
products.body_html:
Grey-blue seiryu with sharp fissures and white veining — the classic iwagumi stone. Sold as a 5 kg pack made up of small pieces.

  • 5 kg is enough for a single focal arrangement in a 45–60 cm tank, or a supporting group in something larger.
  • Every piece is different. Stone is graded by weight, not shape, so the exact set you receive will vary.
  • Seiryu raises hardness. It is a carbonate rock and it will lift GH and KH over time. Fine for most community plants and shrimp that like harder water; check first if you keep soft-water species.

faqs.q: How many pieces will I get?
faqs.a: It is sold by weight rather than count, so we cannot promise a number. Expect several small pieces rather than one large feature stone.

products.title: Spider Wood - Centrepiece Set
products.body_html:
Natural spider wood driftwood pieces. Branching root-like tendrils and fine twisting branches for planted-tank centrepieces.

  • Plug: 5-20cm

faqs.q: Will it need soaking?
faqs.a: Almost certainly. Most spider wood floats until waterlogged and leaches tannins that tint the water for a few weeks. The manufacturer makes no pre-soaking claim, so assume it is untreated — boil or soak it before scaping.

products.title: Master Water Test Kit — pH, Ammonia, Nitrite
products.body_html:
A liquid reagent kit covering the three parameters that actually matter while a tank is cycling: pH, ammonia and nitrite. Roughly 100 tests of each.

  • Liquid reagents, not strips. Slower to use and considerably more accurate, which is what you want when you are deciding whether it is safe to add fish.
  • Three parameters, ~100 tests each. About 300 tests in total.
  • Covers the cycle. Ammonia and nitrite are the two that spike and then fall as a filter matures; pH tells you whether anything has destabilised.

Not included: nitrate, GH or KH. An earlier version of this listing said the kit covered those. It does not — they are separate kits.

faqs.q: Does it test nitrate, GH or KH?
faqs.a: No. This listing previously claimed it covered nitrate and GH/KH. It does not — the kit our supplier ships is the three-parameter version. Those are separate kits and we would rather correct the listing than have you discover it after a water change.

products.title: Digital pH Pen Meter
products.body_html:
A pocket pH pen for freshwater tanks. Reads 0.00–14.00 pH to 0.1 resolution, runs on two 1.5 V cells, and calibrates against standard buffer powders.

  • pH only. This pen does not measure TDS. An earlier version of this listing said it did; it does not, and we have corrected it.
  • 0.1 pH resolution across the full 0–14 range — enough to track a CO2 swing or a KH change day to day.
  • Two-point calibration against standard buffer sachets, which is what keeps a cheap pen honest over time.

faqs.q: Does this measure TDS?
faqs.a: No. This listing previously said it did — that was wrong and we have corrected it. The unit our supplier ships is a pH-only pen. If you need TDS you need a separate meter, and we would rather lose the sale than send you the wrong tool.

faqs.q: How often does it need calibrating?
faqs.a: Monthly for most tanks, or any time a reading looks implausible. Calibration sachets are cheap and the pen drifts without them.

products.title: Test Strips — 9 in 1, 100 Count
products.body_html:
Nine-parameter dip strips including pH, free chlorine, nitrite, nitrate, total alkalinity and hardness. 100-strip pack.

  • Weight: 0.1kg

faqs.q: How do these compare to a liquid kit?
faqs.a: Faster and less precise. Strips are good for a quick weekly check; use a liquid reagent kit when you are cycling a tank or chasing a specific problem.
